drivingQuestion: Is the wooden leg susceptible to midras impurity?
outcomeNote: Each proof is deflected; no ruling.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ — דִּתְנַן: עֲגָלָה שֶׁל קָטָן — טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס. וְאַבָּיֵי אֲמַר: הָתָם סָמֵיךְ עִילָּוֵיהּ, הָכָא לָא סָמֵיךְ עִילָּוֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rava said: From where do I» derive to «say» this halakha? «As we learned» in a mishna: «The wagon of a» small «child» utilized to teach him to walk (Tosafot) «is» subject to «ritual impurity» imparted by «treading,» since its purpose is to lean on it. «And Abaye said:» The two cases are not comparable. «There,» in the case of the wagon, «he leans» all his weight «on it; here,» in the case of the wooden leg, «he does not lean» all his weight «on it.»

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ — דְּתַנְיָא: מַקֵּל שֶׁל זְקֵנִים טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם!
segments.en: «Abaye said: From where do I» derive to «say» this halakha? «As it was taught» in a baraita: «A» walking «stick,» typically used by the «elderly, is pure,» i.e., incapable of becoming ritually impure «from any» form of ritual impurity. Apparently, an object upon which one does not lean all his weight is not subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading.
«And» how does «Rava» respond to this proof? He says that there is a distinction between the cases: «There,» in the case of a walking stick used by the elderly,

segments.he: לְתָרוֹצֵי סוּגְיָא עֲבִידָא, הָכָא — לִסְמוֹךְ עִילָּוֵיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא, וְסָמֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ.
segments.en: «it is made» merely «to align his steps» and straighten his posture. He does not completely lean all his weight on it. «Here,» in the case of a wooden leg, «it is made to lean on, and» in fact «he leans» all his weight «on it.»
